subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Electric Propulsion: Slow Thrust, Long Reach
description: One-minute skill: Electric Propulsion: Slow Thrust, Long Reach.

hook.text: Ion engines produce the thrust of a sheet of paper resting on your hand. Yet they've propelled spacecraft across the solar system.

buildup.text: Ion engines ionize xenon gas and accelerate it with electric fields. Exhaust velocity is ten times higher than chemical rockets.

discovery.text: What they lack in thrust, they make up in duration. An ion engine can fire continuously for years, slowly building enormous speed.

twist.text: NASA's Dawn spacecraft used ion engines to orbit two different bodies — Vesta and Ceres. No chemical rocket could have done both.

climax.text: Hall-effect thrusters now power Starlink satellites. Electric propulsion is mainstream for station-keeping and orbit raising.

punchline.text: Whisper-thin thrust. Years of patience. Farther than any chemical rocket.

quiz.question: Why can ion engines reach higher speeds than chemical rockets despite low thrust?
options: Ion engines use nuclear fuel that stores more energy per gram than chemicals
They fire continuously for years, slowly building enormous speed over time
Electric fields create zero-friction exhaust that transfers energy more directly
